name: Ruthless Prioritization
definition: To focus on what we must win, we give up what we want to do. Laser focus requires courage and confidence. Fast iteration and high-quality execution begin with laser focus.

rows.situation: When the list has more bets than the team can fund
rows.under: Funds them all at 20 percent and wins none of them.
rows.justRight: Picks the few that must be won, resources them fully, and says no to the rest out loud.
rows.over: Cuts to a single bet and leaves the company with no second move.

rows.situation: When the work being cut is genuinely good
rows.under: Keeps it because it is good, not because it must be won.
rows.justRight: Kills good work to fund essential work, and tells the team why it was good and still cut.
rows.over: Cuts good work so often that nothing survives long enough to compound.

rows.under: Adds it. The plan grows and the date does not move.
rows.justRight: Names what comes off the list to make room, or declines the new thing.
rows.over: Refuses everything new on principle, including the thing that has genuinely changed the picture.

rows.situation: When the request comes from someone senior
rows.under: Takes it on because of who asked.
rows.justRight: Asks what it displaces, and takes that answer back to the person who asked.
rows.over: Treats every senior request as noise and stops listening upward.

rows.situation: When saying no will be unpopular
rows.under: Says maybe, and lets the work quietly rot instead.
rows.justRight: Says no clearly, once, with the reason, so there is no ambiguity about what is not happening.
rows.over: Enjoys saying no. Refusal becomes an identity rather than a tool.

rows.situation: When a shipping project keeps growing
rows.under: Accepts every addition and the launch slips again.
rows.justRight: Holds the smallest version that wins, and writes down what comes after launch.
rows.over: Cuts so far that what ships does not win anything.
